acceptance.accepted_history_rule: Only the event exactly anchored by CURRENT.latest_event commit+path+digest is accepted history.
acceptance.candidate_namespace_rule: Artifacts under candidates/ are explicitly non-accepted until a later accepted event references their disposition.
acceptance.duplicate_rule: Existing deterministic claim path is DUPLICATE; do not replace claim and do not advance CURRENT.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Second CURRENT fetch must remain exact v63/blob 6f89f7506721dac689f91514d51d91e52b8022b0/projection digest 2a22b0634fabe2cf35184d68b09137619b448a9535631c677034534148f9283e before one blob-SHA-guarded replacement; final readback must be v64.

campaign_decision.reason: Exact prior-blob SHA reliably rejects stale CURRENT replacement in this branch, but claims and pre-CAS artifacts are separate effects. Readers need an explicit candidate namespace and must treat CURRENT anchoring as the sole acceptance criterion.
campaign_decision.revision: Retain exact CURRENT blob-SHA gating and final readback. Prohibit pre-CAS artifacts from the accepted events namespace; stage them under candidates/ with NON_ACCEPTED status. Only CURRENT.latest_event exact commit+path+digest denotes accepted history; preserve failed candidates and conflicts as evidence.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is sequential orchestration, not true simultaneous execution. The candidate, claims, accepted event, CURRENT replacement, stale write attempt, conflict receipt, readbacks, and Slack post are separate effects. A candidate can remain orphaned; CURRENT anchoring is a repository convention, not a database constraint. Git provides a branch-local single-file blob-SHA precondition, not cross-file atomicity, isolation, linearizability, fairness, exactly-once execution, cross-branch exclusion, force-push safety, or Slack atomicity.

probe.name: PRECURRENT_CANDIDATE_THEN_STALE_BLOB_CAS_REJECTION_V4

contender_b.post_advance_rule: PRESERVE_CANDIDATE_AND_CONFLICT_RECEIPT; DO NOT TREAT CANDIDATE AS ACCEPTED

probe.result: Contender B candidate was created and read back before A advanced. A is the accepted transition. After A v64 readback, B must attempt CURRENT replacement with stale v63 blob SHA and be rejected; B candidate remains explicitly non-accepted evidence.

canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete claims, candidate, accepted event, or conflict receipt. If v64 is later invalid, append a compensating transition from the then-current exact version and update CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
